chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Writing with Una Mae Carlisle
summary: McRae recalls working weeks on each song with pianist Una Mae Carlisle, who wrote "Walking by the River"; Welburn adds her death in 1956.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Teddy, you've given me a copy of a list of things that involve song titles and writers -- actually, co-writers with you.
Yeah.
People like Sid Wyche --
Yeah.
Joyce Ann Bennett, Charles Singleton, Dorsly Terry.
Then there were things here by Henry Glover. There's Una Mae Carlisle and Johnny Bradford, teamed with you on a song, "Who's Kissing Who."
Yeah.
Could you tell me some things about Una Mae Carlisle? You met her --
Una Mae Carlisle, yeah. We did -- oh, my goodness. She was a great artist, you know.
She wrote that song "Walking By The River."
That's right.
Remember that big -- she was
a good artist.
So we decided to do some things together and it called for (inaudible) quite a lot of records. I think I wrote for her for a whole month.
Then we would write, you know, like --
Now that's what I liked about her. You couldn't just come in and write a song just for a couple of days and say this is good, (inaudible).
She would work -- you would have to work with her on a song maybe two or three weeks before she would turn it loose, you know.
She wrote this thing, "You're Getting Old Before My Time," and a few other things (inaudible) did with her.
She was from Lima --
Ohio, yeah. Out around -- that's (inaudible) Ohio --
Very talented young lady. I think she played good piano (inaudible) --
Yeah, she was Fats Waller's protege for awhile.
Yeah. Very good. I wrote

for her about two or three months. We were just, you know, off and on.
Whenever she was in town, we'd get together and write something else, like that, you know. Go by her house.
You know, like we come by, we're gonna do something tonight. We go by and write for maybe two or three hours. And maybe next week we'll finish it up -- things like that.
